title: Reap the whole process tree of a killed role or check
lead: When ork kills a role or a check (hung watchdog, owner stop, timeout, restart reconcile), it also kills the processes the role started that left the role's process group, so `go test` and its test binaries do not stay behind as orphans that share the worktree.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
In wave 4 (2026-11-02, `.scratch/v11/wave4-friction.md`, F15 and F16) the "hung" kill of the S207 implementer killed the process group but left `go test -race -json ./... -timeout=20m` (pid 71084, ppid 1) and its test binaries running for more than two hours. They used CPU while the next attempt ran, and shared the worktree. At 23:02 EST test binaries from the 19:55 check were still alive (state U) while a new check run started its own. The owner had to find and kill them by hand.

Verified against HEAD of main (9202ba8); anchors re-checked on 2026-11-07 at a1114e2:

- Every vendor adapter and `clirun.Run` put the child in its own process group (`clirun.OwnProcessGroup`, `internal/clirun/procgroup_unix.go:14-25`: `Setpgid`, and a `Cancel` that sends SIGKILL to `-pid`). Callers: `internal/agent/codex/codex.go:230`, `internal/agent/claude/run.go:61`, `internal/agent/grok/grok.go:286` (in grok's `Run`, `grok.go:265`), `internal/clirun/clirun.go:139`. After the child exits, `KillGroup` sends SIGKILL to the same group (`procgroup_unix.go:27-33`; used at `codex.go:239`, `claude/run.go:71`, `grok/grok.go:295`, `clirun.go:145`).
- The hung watchdog kills nothing itself: it ends the round's context, and the adapter's `Cancel` does the group kill (`internal/engine/watchdog.go:14-19`, `internal/engine/round.go:372-376`).
- `Engine.Reconcile` kills only the recorded role process group, by `syscall.Kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)` (`internal/engine/recover.go:64`, `internal/engine/proc_unix.go:30-43`).
- A signal to `-pgid` reaches only processes still in that group. A process that called `setsid` or `setpgid` (a tool runner or sandbox wrapper inside the vendor CLI may do this; I could not check what Codex or Claude do) is outside the group, and once its parent dies it has ppid 1. That is the state the log shows (F16: ppid 1). So the group kill is not enough for such a tree. No code path walks the process tree.
- I could not verify from the log or from the code why the 71084 process was outside the group, nor whether it was still a descendant of the vendor process at kill time. The first Implement step reproduces the escape with a test helper, so the fix is proven by a test and not assumed from the log.
- `docs/design.md:666-675` says only process groups named by run records are killed; `docs/design.md:880-881` says "it never kills a process it did not start". Killing descendants of a recorded role is a change to that wording (owner question Q2 in the manifest).

Overlap: S235 (`sleep-wake-awareness`, done) removed the main cause of hung kills (a wake). A real hang, an owner stop and a check timeout still kill, so reaping stays needed.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/clirun/proctree_unix.go` (new; `go:build unix`; the process table snapshot and `KillTree`).
- `internal/clirun/proctree_other.go` (new; `go:build !unix`; no-ops).
- `internal/clirun/proctree_unix_test.go` (new).
- `internal/clirun/procgroup_unix.go:14-33` (`OwnProcessGroup`'s `Cancel` and `KillGroup` snapshot and kill the tree).
- `internal/clirun/clirun_test.go:30` (new helper case `spawn-setsid` in `helperMain`) and `:79` (the new tests beside `TestTimeoutKillsTheProcessGroup`).
- No change in the vendor adapters: codex, claude and grok (`internal/agent/grok/grok.go:286`, `:295`) all go through `clirun.OwnProcessGroup` and `clirun.KillGroup`, so they get the tree kill from `procgroup_unix.go`.
- `internal/engine/proc_unix.go:30-43` (`osProc.Kill` also kills the descendants of the group leader when the leader is alive).
- `internal/engine/proc_unix_test.go` (new test beside `TestOSProcKillsAProcessGroupAndRefusesToKillOthers`).
- `docs/design.md:662-676` (reconcile), `:876-895` (Hung role item), `docs/state.md:415-418` (lost pause). (`docs/boundaries.md` has no sentence about killing processes: `rg -n "kill|process group" docs/boundaries.md` finds nothing, so it needs no change.)
- `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased entry, marked *proposed*; add it last).

No UI: no `internal/tui`, no golden view, no CLI output.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/clirun/proctree_unix_test.go` (pure parsing, no real processes):

- `TestParseProcTable`: the text of `ps -axo pid=,ppid=` (leading spaces, several rows, one blank line, one malformed row) gives the pid to ppid map and skips the bad row. It fails first because the parser does not exist.
- `TestDescendantsFollowsParentsTransitively`: child, grandchild and great-grandchild of pid 100 are returned; an unrelated pid 200 and its child are not.
- `TestDescendantsNeverReturnsOneOrSelf`: pid 1, pid 0, the test process and its parent are dropped even if the table lists them under the root.
- `TestDescendantsOfAnUnknownPidIsEmpty`.

In `internal/clirun/clirun_test.go` (real processes, the existing helper pattern):

- `TestTimeoutKillsADescendantThatLeftTheProcessGroup`: helper case `spawn-setsid` starts a grandchild with `SysProcAttr{Setsid: true}` (so it is outside the group), prints its pid and blocks. `Run` with a 1.5 s timeout ends in `*TimeoutError`, and the grandchild is dead within 5 s. It fails first because `Cancel` kills only `-pid`, so the setsid grandchild survives (the helper's `block` case sleeps 30 s, so a failing run leaves nothing long-lived).
- `TestParentCancelKillsADescendantThatLeftTheProcessGroup`: the same with the parent context cancelled instead of a timeout (the owner stop and the hung watchdog end the context this way).
- `TestKillTreeIgnoresAFailedProcessTable`: a `ps` that is missing or fails (a function variable for the table reader, set by the test) leaves the group kill working and returns no error and no panic.
- `TestTimeoutKillsTheProcessGroup` and `TestGrandchildHoldingStdoutAfterExitIsKilled` (existing) still pass unchanged.

In `internal/engine/proc_unix_test.go`:

- `TestOSProcKillAlsoKillsDescendantsOutsideTheGroup`: start a leader in its own group (`Setpgid`) that starts a `Setsid` child (a helper binary or `sh -c`; use the pattern the package already uses, or skip with `t.Skip` when the shell cannot do it). `osProc.Kill(leaderPGID)` kills both. Fails first because `Kill` signals only `-pgid`.
- `TestOSProcKillOfADeadLeaderStillKillsTheGroup`: no leader, only members of the group: the group kill works as before.
- `TestOSProcRejectsUnsafeGroupsBeforeSignalling` (existing) still passes: the tree walk must not run for pgid 0, 1, negative or ork's own group.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
The steps follow the owner's answers of 2026-11-02 (interactive question): the tree is found from a `ps` snapshot taken at kill time, and `docs/design.md` (the rule that ork never kills a process it did not start) is changed to cover the descendants of a role.

1. Reproduce first. Add the `spawn-setsid` helper case and `TestTimeoutKillsADescendantThatLeftTheProcessGroup` and run it: it must fail by leaving the grandchild alive. If it passes on this platform, stop and report to the owner (the escape is then not what the log shows).
2. `internal/clirun/proctree_unix.go`: `processTable()` runs `ps -axo pid=,ppid=` with a 2-second timeout through `exec.CommandContext` (no `clirun.Run`, which would put `ps` in a group of its own and is not needed) and parses it with `parseProcTable`. `descendants(table, root)` returns every transitive child of `root`, never pid 0, 1, the current process or its parent. `KillTree(pid int)` takes the table, then SIGKILLs the group `-pid` and then each descendant pid; ESRCH is not an error. If `ps` fails, `KillTree` does the group kill only. The table reader is a package variable so a test can replace it (a `ps` snapshot works on macOS and Linux and needs only the standard library).
3. `internal/clirun/procgroup_unix.go`: `Cancel` calls `KillTree(cmd.Process.Pid)` instead of the single `syscall.Kill` and still returns `os.ErrProcessDone` when the group is gone. The snapshot must be taken before the group kill, because after it the escaped children are reparented to pid 1 and no longer reachable from the leader. `KillGroup` (after the leader exited) cannot walk a tree that is already detached, so it stays a group kill; say so in its comment.
4. `proctree_other.go`: `KillTree` is a no-op on non-unix platforms; `OwnProcessGroup` there is unchanged.
5. `internal/engine/proc_unix.go`: `osProc.Kill` keeps its guards (pgid 1 or less, ork's own group) and, when the leader pid `pgid` is alive, calls the same snapshot and kills the group and the descendants. Keep the injectable `signal` field working: the descendants are signalled through it too.
6. Docs: `docs/design.md` reconcile and Hung role items get one sentence: ork also kills the processes the role started that left its group, found from the role's pid before the kill (*proposed*); state the limit: a process already reparented to pid 1 before the kill is not found. Change the "never kills a process it did not start" sentence as the owner decided. Do not paste the contract text.
7. Do not touch the watchdog, the 30-minute limit, the vendor adapters (codex, claude and grok already call `clirun`), `internal/tui`, or `Engine.Reconcile`'s logic beyond what `osProc.Kill` does.
8. Add the `CHANGELOG.md` entry last, under `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed*: "Kill the descendants of a killed role or check that left its process group."

Owner decision (2026-11-09, interactive question): the orchestrator runs the four Check lines the implementer sandbox cannot run (the -race -count=3 line, both GOOS vet lines, the ps line); the implementer runs the rest [process.s236-check-lines].

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=3 ./internal/clirun ./internal/engine -run 'Tree|Descend|OSProc|Timeout|Cancel'`.
- `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go -C WORKTREE vet ./internal/clirun ./internal/engine` and `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go -C WORKTREE vet ./internal/clirun ./internal/engine` (the build tags must hold on both, whichever the host is; the release workflow builds darwin and linux archives).
- `ps -axo pid=,ppid=` on the host (macOS or Linux) prints the two columns the parser expects (run it once, name the OS, report the first lines).
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] Start a run whose role runs a long `go test`, `ork stop` it, and confirm with `ps -axo pid,ppid,etime,command | rg 'go test|\.test'` that no `go test` or test binary of that worktree remains.
